hook.line: You walk into the café and find your friend sitting there, when you were sure he had an exam. English says "Wait, don't you have an exam?" Spanish asks it in the past tense, and the tone is part of the message.
hook.en: Didn't you have an exam tomorrow?

examples.en: Didn't you have an exam tomorrow? (to a friend)
But hadn't you left? (to a friend)
Weren't you working today? (to a stranger, formal)
Didn't you all live in Medellín?
Weren't you a vegetarian? (to a man, a friend)

rule:
When something does not match what you had understood, Spanish asks about it in the imperfect, even if the thing is about today or tomorrow. The past tense says "this is what I had in my head". It is not about time.

*¿Tú no tenías un examen mañana?*

It shows surprise, and often a mild reproach: the real message is "so why aren't you studying?" Don't just answer *sí, lo tenía*. Answer the point: *Sí, pero ya estudié.*

The usual frame: *¿(Pero) tú no + imperfect…?*
smallPrint: Teachers call this the imperfect of surprise: the imperfect used for a fact you believed and now doubt.

options: Wait, don't you have an exam tomorrow? I thought you did.
Did you not have an exam yesterday?
You won't have an exam tomorrow.
But won't you leave?
But hadn't you left? (and yet you are here)
But didn't you stay?
Isn't Vale coming tomorrow?
Did Vale come yesterday?
Wasn't Vale supposed to come today?
Didn't you all live in Medellín? I thought so.
Don't you all want to live in Medellín?
Will you all live in Medellín?
Are you going to be a vegetarian?
Weren't you a vegetarian? I thought you were.
You were never a vegetarian.
You aren't working today, are you?
Did you work today, sir?
Weren't you working today, sir?
Wasn't Mariana in Cali? I thought she was.
Is Mariana going to Cali?
Mariana was never in Cali.
Do you want to go to the movies?
Didn't you want to go to the movies?
You didn't go to the movies.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *tienes* or *tenías*, to a friend you are surprised to see: "Don't you have an exam tomorrow? (I thought you did)"
accept: ¿Pero tú no tenías un examen mañana?
yourTurn.why: The imperfect *tenías* shows you are surprised; *tienes* would be a plain question.

yourTurn.prompt: To a friend: "But hadn't you left?"
yourTurn.why: *Te habías ido* is "you had gone", and the *no* makes it a surprised question.
*Venía* is the imperfect of *venir*, used for what you understood was planned.

yourTurn.prompt: To a group: "Didn't you all live in Medellín?"
Make it formal: *¿Tú no trabajabas hoy?*
To Hernando, formally: "Weren't you a taxi driver?"
yourTurn.why: *Era* is the imperfect of *ser* and fits both *usted* and *él*.

yourTurn.prompt: To a male friend: "Weren't you a vegetarian?"
yourTurn.why: *Eras* is the *tú* form, and *vegetariano* is masculine because you are talking to a man.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The present is a neutral question; the imperfect tells your friend you are surprised.
The preterite means a finished event; for "I thought you had" use the imperfect.
The question is really a reproach, so answer the point and not the tense.

personal: Think of the last time you were surprised to see someone. Ask them out loud: *¿Tú no…?* with the imperfect.
